thread_text:
maria-support: Hey team — escalated ticket INC-4129 from Acme: streaming responses over SSE are frequently disconnecting and sometimes returning only a partial JSON payload. Customer says SDK iterators hang on reconnect. Seen in Python and Node.

sam-runtime: Ack. Any quick repro from the customer?

maria-support: They included a curl repro: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-large"
```
They say stream returns a few "data: { ... }\n\n" events then the connection closes unexpectedly. Browser clients attempt to reconnect but get an empty final event and our Python iterator stops iterating.

jinx-py-sdk: Sounds like the iterator is interpreting a read() with done=True as a final done for the whole stream, instead of waiting for server reconnects. Which SDK version?

maria-support: Customer on py-sdk 0.8.1. They also reported that when they proxy the request through Cloudflare the disconnects are worse.

alex-js-sdk: For Node/Browser, EventSource auto-reconnects, but our SDK wraps fetch/readable-stream. We had a regression in 0.11.0 where we prematurely call controller.close() when the underlying stream yields an empty Uint8Array. Possible related.

chris-eng-oncall: Can someone capture a sample server-side trace for that request id? I can correlate with LB logs. Ticket includes timestamp 2025-10-12T15:22:03Z.

devops-bot: Found LB trace: request 7f3a22 -> backend returned 200 then connection closed at 2.1s. No 4xx/5xx. Upstream log shows flush of bytes then socket close.

jinx-py-sdk: Two likely culprits: (1) gzip/brotli proxy negotiation causing the stream to be buffered and then closed when proxy rewrites headers, or (2) our Python iterator using requests.iter_lines() which can drop final partial lines if the server doesn't end with a newline.

maria-support: They said server sends SSE events without an extra blank line at the end sometimes.

sam-runtime: We should also check that our runtime sets `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and doesn't add Content-Length. Proxies that add Content-Length will kill SSE semantics. Chris, any proxies adding content-length?

chris-eng-oncall: Checked nginx sidecar config: `proxy_set_header Connection "";` and `proxy_buffering off;` set. But there is an intermediate edge CDN that sometimes inserts `Content-Length` for responses under 2kB. Suspicious.

alex-js-sdk: Ok maybe combination: CDN buffers small responses -> inserts Content-Length -> closes stream early -> SDK sees stream end. For Node fetch wrapper we treat any end-of-stream as terminal. We need to make reconnect-friendlier: if socket closes with status 200 and last event didn't contain "[DONE]" sentinel, attempt transparent reconnect and resume via `?cursor=` param if supported.

jinx-py-sdk: For Python SDK, short-term fix: change iterator behaviour so that a transient socket close (no 4xx/5xx) triggers up to N reconnect attempts within a short window before raising StopIteration. Also ensure parser tolerates partial last line (buffer until next data). Example patch idea: 
```python
# pseudo
buffer = b''
for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
    buffer += chunk
    while b"\n\n" in buffer:
        event, buffer = buffer.split(b"\n\n", 1)
        yield parse_event(event)
# on socket close, keep buffer in memory and if not empty try reconnect and send `cursor` to resume
```

maria-support: Customer also reported that when they used raw curl with `--no-buffer` the stream was more stable. Could be gzip or chunk buffering.

sam-runtime: Action plan: 1) eng-runtime to verify response headers & edge CDN behaviour and add optional SSE keepalive comment frames (":\n") every 15s. 2) py-sdk team to implement tolerant iterator + reconnect heuristics. 3) js-sdk to revert 0.11.0 aggressive close behaviour and add resume logic. 4) support to provide customer with temporary workaround (disable CDN caching / add `Cache-Control: no-transform` if possible).

chris-eng-oncall: I'll add keepalive comments from runtime side — we can stream a `:heartbeat\n\n` every 10s. That reduces intermediate proxies from thinking connection is idle. Rolling patch to canary now.

alex-js-sdk: I'll open PR to revert the controller.close() change and add a small TTL reconnect logic for fetch streams. Also adding tests for partial event sequences and final-chunkless events.

jinx-py-sdk: I'll draft a patch for 0.8.2 that buffers partial lines and retries reconnect twice with exponential backoff. Need guidance from runtime on resume cursor API — does the server persist KV cache for SSE?

sam-runtime: We support a `stream_cursor` query param for resumable streams (recent rollout). We need to document it and enable it for public models. I'll post the spec in eng-runtime channel.

customer-success: I already told the customer the short-term workaround: disable CDN transform and use raw websocket fallback if possible. They asked for ETA.

maria-support: ETA requested: can eng teams provide rough timelines?

chris-eng-oncall: Keepalive patch to canary within 2hrs, monitor for reduction in disconnects.

alex-js-sdk: Revert PR + tests today, patch release 0.11.1 by EOD.

jinx-py-sdk: Py patch targeted for tomorrow morning, release 0.8.2. Will include note in changelog about streaming robustness.

sam-runtime: I'll follow up with docs for stream_cursor and add an opt-in `auto_resume=true` flag on the API. That should cover most customer cases.

maria-support: Great. I'll inform the customer and keep ticket open until we verify improvements. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 

devops-bot: Canary deployment started: runtime/keepalive:v2 -> canary hosts (3/3). Monitoring 30m aggregated metrics.

maria-support: Logging note — if you need to reproduce locally, customer supplied a minimal Node repro: 
```js
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-large');
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('evt', e.data);
es.onerror = (e) => console.log('err', e);
```
They also sent a Python reproducible case using requests where the iterator stops after two events.

sam-runtime: Good. We'll track this thread and cc when fixes land. If anyone finds stack traces or weird Content-Encoding interactions post-canary, ping me.

maria-support: Thanks — closing loop with customer after runtime canary and SDK patches are out.
